sections.h2: What the Fulton County Recorder does
sections.html:
The Recorder indexes and files each land document in the county. Buyers use the index to trace past owners, and lenders use it to see what debts attach to a parcel.

West of Toledo, Fulton County is part of that metro area. County business happens in Wauseon, including filings for homes in Archbold, Delta, Swanton, Fayette, Lyons and Metamora.

The Recorder is at 152 S. Fulton St., Suite 175, Wauseon, OH 43567. The counter serves the public on weekdays from half past eight until half past four, and the number is (419) 337-9232.

  • Recorder: Suite 175, where a deed ends up.
  • Auditor: Suite 165, same building, where it starts. Real estate questions go to (419) 337-9200.
  • Land records search: linked from the county's Records Search page, handy for finding earlier deeds and mortgages.

The Recorder page also carries a Real Property Conveyance Standards PDF plus printable plats and land surveys. Read them before you draft a legal description.

sections.h2: Steps before the deed reaches the Recorder
sections.html:
The county's conveyance standards put every legal description through the same review. The aim is to catch visible errors and describe the parcel properly for tax purposes. Unusual cases are sent to a panel of the County Engineer, the Auditor and the Planning Director.

  1. Draft the deed, copying the legal description from the most recent recorded deed.
  2. Have it acknowledged by a notary. R.C. 5301.01 also allows a judge, court clerk, county auditor, county engineer or mayor.
  3. Take it to Suite 165 for the description review, the conveyance fee and the transfer.
  4. Then walk it to Suite 175 and pay the recording fee.

Ohio's transfer tax statute makes the grantor settle with the Auditor first, so do not reverse the order. Ask the Recorder which endorsement it expects to see.

The rate is $4.00 for every thousand dollars of total consideration, with the amount rounded up to the next $100, and a $0.50 per parcel transfer fee. The Auditor's own example turns $100,001 into $100,100 and reaches $400.40.

That figure has two state layers. A statement-of-value fee of ten cents per $100 comes from R.C. 319.54(G)(3), and a county may add up to thirty cents per $100 under R.C. 322.02. The grantor pays when the deed is delivered.

Certain transfers owe no fee under R.C. 319.54(G)(3):

  • a gift to a spouse, or from parent to child;
  • a deal with no money or other valuable consideration that is also not a gift;
  • a no-money conveyance among heirs or devisees of a single decedent;
  • a trustee returning property to the grantor of a revocable trust.

If your sale looks like one of these, check with the Auditor's real estate office before assuming a fee is owed.

Recording fees are set by the state, and half of each fee funds the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. A printed side counts as a page. A county can tack on a preservation surcharge of no more than $5.00 per document, so call the Fulton Recorder for the final amount before you mail a check.

A standard layout applies to any deed you give the Recorder under R.C. 317.114. Miss it and the deed is still accepted, at the cost of another $10 base fee and $10 housing trust fee.

  • Ten point type or larger.
  • Paper at least letter size, up to 14 inches long.
  • Black or blue ink, with no highlighting.
  • An inch of blank margin on each side and at the bottom of every page.
  • A three inch blank band at the top of page one for the Engineer, Auditor and Recorder endorsements, then one and a half inches at the top of later pages.

Court and tax-authority papers, plats, state and federal documents, and anything signed before July 1, 2009 are outside the rule.

The April 2020 count was 42,713 people, and the July 2025 estimate of 41,853 is down 2.0 percent. Of all homes, 80.2 percent are owner-occupied, with a median value of $191,000 for those. The county gave out 57 building permits in 2025, and median household income is $72,864.

Across 405 square miles of land, at roughly 105 residents per square mile, parcels range from farm acreage to village lots in Archbold and Wauseon to homes in any of its twelve townships.

sections.h2: Other items in the land records
sections.html:
Expect a title search to look past the latest deed. At a sheriff's sale, liens are paid in order out of the proceeds and then cancelled against the property, but a federal lien survives and stays on file with the Recorder. Buyers at such sales must check each lien themselves.

  • Mortgages, releases and assignments are kept in the very office that holds the deed.
  • Filing a federal tax lien costs $5.00, and releasing one costs $3.00.
  • There is no charge to record military discharge papers.
  • Plats and condominium drawings are charged by area, ten cents per square inch, with a $40.00 minimum.

Search the parcel in the Recorder's land records and in the Auditor's property search before setting a closing date.

sections.h2: Tax rules a seller should check
sections.html:
Bills arrive twice a year, due in February and July. The lien date is January 1, and billing trails by a year. A bill paid in 2025 covered tax year 2024 and reflected the home's worth as 2025 began.

  • Owner-occupied reduction: residences only, never applied by itself. Enroll at (419) 337-9200.
  • Value complaints: file with the Board of Revision any time from January 1 to March 31.
  • Payments and mailing address changes for tax bills: the Treasurer handles both, not the Auditor.

Ask the Fulton County Treasurer for a payoff figure on the parcel, and have the title company spell out who covers which bill.

sections.h2: Selling for cash in Fulton County
sections.html: With cash there is no lender, but the route through the courthouse is unchanged: signed, notarized deed to Suite 165, then to Suite 175. Stick to the layout rules above to avoid extra fees. Because payment is part of the filing, phone ahead for the exact total, as the county decides the preservation surcharge. Also have a photo ID, your latest tax bill and any payoff letter ready, so the title agent can finish the same day.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax collected by the Fulton County Recorder?
faqs.a: Not by the Recorder, which collects only the recording fee. The $4.00 per $1,000 conveyance fee and the $0.50 per parcel transfer fee go to the Auditor, paid by the grantor before filing.

faqs.q: Can a Fulton County deed skip the Auditor and go straight to recording?
faqs.a: No. Visit the Auditor first. The grantor pays there under R.C. 322.02 before the Recorder sees the deed, and each legal description is reviewed under the county standards.

faqs.q: What hours does the Wauseon Recorder keep?
faqs.a: It is open on weekdays, half past eight until half past four, at Suite 175, 152 S. Fulton St. Call (419) 337-9232. The Auditor is down the hall in Suite 165.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed has a small font or thin margins?
faqs.a: It will be filed, with $10 more in base fee and $10 more in housing trust fee under R.C. 317.114. Court papers, plats, state and federal documents and instruments signed before July 1, 2009 are exempt.

faqs.q: Where do I send a complaint that my Fulton County home is overvalued?
faqs.a: Send it to the Board of Revision by way of the Auditor's real estate office, (419) 337-9200. Complaints are accepted January 1 to March 31, and staff can mail a form or direct you to the printable copy.
